extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent examiners, patent applicants, and patent attorneys/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and examining patent specifications and claims under the Korean Patent Act, covering enablement, description method, background art, industrial applicability, claims format, and examiner notification procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement requirement (practicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an embodiment related to the claims is deemed different from the embodiment disclosed in the description and the invention related to the claims cannot be practiced only with the embodiments disclosed in the description, an examiner shall notify a ground for rejection in violation of Article 42(3)(i) of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When notifying enablement violations, the examiner shall specify the violation and the corresponding claims. For applications filed after Jan 1, 2015, enablement-type deficiencies may be proposed for amendment under Article 46 rather than immediate invalidation. If description meets Article 21(3) layout but is not detailed/clear enough to practice the claimed invention, notify under Article 42(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims supported by description (written support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall be supported by the description of the invention (Article 42(4)(i)). An examiner shall determine support based on whether a person skilled in the art can figure out the subject matters corresponding to the claims from the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine support by whether the claimed subject matter departs from the scope a skilled person would grasp from the description, not by literal identity. If claims recite subject matter neither disclosed nor implied, or terms differ creating ambiguity, or claimed functional means lack corresponding specific configuration, notify lack of support. Examples include numerical limits not disclosed and claims directed to a motor type not disclosed in the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of terms between description and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the terms used in the description and the claims do not clearly match, an examiner shall notify a ground for rejection citing violation of Article 42(4)(i) since the invention recited in the claims is not supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If technical terms differ or are ambiguous so correspondence between description and claims is unclear, the examiner should raise rejection. Where differing terms can be reconciled by common general knowledge, claims may still be supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description method requirement — required sections
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle the description shall contain: title of the invention, technical field, background art, prior art literature, brief description of the drawing(s), summary of invention, detailed description for practicing invention, industrial applicability, consignment number, and sequence listing free text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections need not be separately prepared if their contents are understood from the overall description. Where some sections cannot be filled due to nature of the invention, omission may be acceptable (e.g., serendipitous composition where objectives/solutions are unnecessary). Each section should be clear and precise enough for a skilled person to understand and reproduce the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of description (technical disclosure and reproducibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must disclose the invention so a third party can easily understand the invention considering the level of skill in the art at filing and reproduce/practice it; it should show unresolved tasks in the technical field and how those tasks are solved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method of description should clarify technical matter and scope sought for patent protection so a third party can understand the invention by the specification alone. This aligns with internationally adopted specification-writing practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical field disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The technical field of the invention shall be stated clearly and briefly; related technical fields should be disclosed if possible. At least one technical field should be indicated unless a skilled person can understand it without explicit description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may refer to the IPC class if known. Omission is acceptable only where the skilled person can readily identify the field from the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of invention: problems, means, and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary should include the technical problems to be solved, means for solving them, and the effects of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical problems subsection: state the prior-art issue unless a skilled person can infer it or the invention arises from wholly novel ideas. Means subsection: state the type of means used (the invention itself can be the means); may be omitted if the skilled person can understand the solving process from other parts. Effects subsection: state particular superior effects over prior art as far as the applicant knows because such disclosure helps recognize inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description for practicing the invention — completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one detailed description for practicing the invention shall be stated, preferably in various ways so a person skilled in the art can easily figure out how to practice the invention. The detailed technical means themselves shall be stated, not mere functions or effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where multiple technical means exist, explain how they interrelate. Include functions and configuration. In some fields (e.g., computers) function descriptions and interconnections may be more appropriate than hardware configuration. Use standard terms and widely used chemical/mathematical symbols. Where drawings exist, describe them and reference numbers in parentheses after technical terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embodiments: number and types to disclose
rubrics_metrics.description: As many embodiments as possible should be stated; where claims are generic, each representative embodiment corresponding to the generic description should be stated unless a skilled person can infer details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include basic data; where needed, provide comparative and alternative embodiments. Comparative embodiments should be technically closest to the invention and differences among embodiments should be specified. Indicate drawing reference numbers for embodiments described with drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical limitations and experimental details
rubrics_metrics.description: For numerical limitations, the ground for limitation shall be disclosed. When using experimental data, test methods, tools, and conditions must be described in detail so a skilled person can reproduce results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If materials or devices hard to obtain are used, disclose manufacturing process or sources. Lack of reproducibility information may lead to rejection under enablement or description method requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is hard to determine whether the claimed invention is industrially applicable, the utilization method, manufacturing method, or method of industrial applicability shall be stated in the Industrial Applicability section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If industrial applicability can be well inferred from other parts of the specification, additional description may not be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background art: meaning and requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Background art refers to conventional art beneficial in understanding technological implications of the invention and conducting prior art searches and examination. The description shall disclose background art related to the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed after July 1, 2011 failure to disclose background art triggers a notice of rejection under Article 42(3)(ii). Background art must be related to the claimed invention considering technical field, technical problems, solutions, and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background art disclosure details (prior art citation information)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant shall disclose detailed explanation on the background art and information on prior art literature where such background art is disclosed, if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation information should include country of publication, gazette name, publication number, date (for patents), and author, title, publisher, publication date (for non-patent literature). If multiple prior art documents exist, disclose the literature(s) closest to the invention. If an applicant cannot find proper background art (novel idea), disclose closest technical field or difficulty finding background art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate background art examples (illegitimate disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illegitimate background art disclosure includes: no background art described; background art not related to the claimed invention; background art consisting only of basic/general technology that is not beneficial in understanding the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proper background art exists and can be easily searched, mere disclosure of general basic technology is insufficient and may be a ground for rejection. Examiner may suggest appropriate prior art at time of notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to background art rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When a ground for rejection is notified for failure to describe background art, an applicant should amend by adding information on prior art literature in Background or Prior Art Literature, and may submit written argument that the background art is already disclosed in the cited prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the invention is truly novel and no proper background art exists, respond by explaining the novelty and difficulty finding background art in written argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign language and translation issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for specifications written in a foreign language under Article 42(3)(i), where terms are not written in Korean so the description is unclear, an examiner shall give the applicant an opportunity to explain (Article 11(1)(iv)) and return the application; if only part is foreign but content is understandable, do not return—order amendment under Article 46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For priority applications with translation errors, do not notify rejection solely for translation error; notify only when failure to meet description requirements is found in the priority-claiming specification. Examiners should examine thoroughly because amendments to correct translation may risk adding new matter or changing what is practiced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of uncommon technical/academic terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical or academic terms not widely used must be defined in the description; if definitions are unclear or the invention cannot be understood because terms lack definitions or original language/Chinese characters, notify rejection under Article 42(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Chinese characters or original language in brackets where Korean understanding would be impeded. Lack of definition may render the description unclear and non-enabling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of trademarks or product names in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, stating a trademark or product name is not allowed in a specification, but it may be exceptionally allowed where the product can be easily obtained and the trademarked product's quality/composition is unlikely to change the content of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reliance on a specific trademark unless necessary and safe; if used, explain sources or equivalence to ensure reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims formal/format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall include an independent claim and may include dependent claims. Number of claims shall be reasonable to the nature of the invention. A claim referring to another must state the number referred to; multiple dependent claims must not serve as a basis for other multiple dependent claims. Each claim shall be entered on a new line and serial numbers in Arabic figures shall be given in order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow ordering rules: claim from which other claims depend must precede them. Multiple-dependent claim reference to more than one other claim shall be in the alternative. Ensure claim numbering and formatting comply with Enforcement Decree and Presidential Decree provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of invention and claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention recited in the claims is what the applicant regards as their invention for which protection is sought; determination of the invention shall be made based on claim limitations in accordance with the applicant's will. Description and drawings are considered only when claims are indefinite or terms ambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not determine protection scope based on description disclosure beyond claim limitations. Abstract cannot be used to decide protection scope. Examiner should be mindful that improper claims may unfairly limit third-party rights or cause invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: How examiner should notify grounds for rejection for description defects
rubrics_metrics.description: When notifying grounds for rejection citing enablement and description method requirements, any violation shall be specified and notified; especially for enablement, the corresponding claims shall be specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed before Dec 31, 2014, violation of both enablement and description method could be a ground for rejection; for applications filed after Jan 1, 2015, examiners should notify under Article 42(3)(i) and propose amendment under Article 46. If description method requirement is violated but all claimed inventions can still be easily practiced, the description shall be deemed legitimate.
